items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: See, back then playing with Dave Otholomew, we played for, almost identical to the way I play today. He played for all the social clubs, he got a lot of black social clubs, played for all of the high school.

ctx.x: Was that about a certain person? Lavinia.

No, that just was a song. I'll tell you, well, there was a story I recorded. That song, that's the only song that I feel like I stole from somebody in all my career as a musician. Well, I got that song from Blazer Boy. What Blazer Boy's name was? George Stevenson, was that? George Stevenson, I think so. Well, anyway, he used to be at the, at the, not the Tijuana. I went to the hotel around there on, but I was around about three. But anyway, in this place, I went in there one night where Hugh Smith, guitar, Slim,…
Okay, I had a song called Junie Mae. Junie Mae, Junie Mae.

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: I'm talking about from way back with doing the Earl Palmer era with David Tholomew

ctx.x: 86. So we were talking about dramas.

Yeah, well I was talking about the present drummer that I have in my present band today, and I stated just a minute ago that I have been associated with better musicians in all of my days, and I'm talking about from way back with doing the Earl Palmer era with David Tholomew, Ernest MacLange, Salvador Doucette, see these people are musicians, there ain't no F and A's about it. Okay, that's a caliber musician I have dealt with. All the way up my band, the original Untouchables, Larry Marino, Charlie Burbank, and…

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: When I got in the music business and when I went to record, I went to Mr. Levy's office with Dave Bartholomew.

ctx.x: So when did Tommy come to you?

When I got in the music business and when I went to record, I went to Mr. Levy's office with Dave Bartholomew. And we sat down and I signed all these papers. You know, if I had a hit record I wouldn't have got no money I guess. Same way. But anyway, they discussed a professional name. And so he came up with, he said, well let's think of something. And one name always stick in my mind. He said, let's come with something like Memphis Slim or something. And I listened at him tossing names around and then I said,…
Oh, you mean making it a professional name?
